How it works

How the moving cost calculator works

You answer the same questions a mover would ask first. The calculator turns them into a realistic price range for your move.

There's no sign-up and no email gate. If the estimate looks right and you want a firm number, you can ask a specialist to confirm it. If not, you leave with a useful number and nothing else.

What you tell us

  • What you're moving: a home, office, piano, hot tub and more
  • Your moving-from and moving-to ZIP codes
  • Home size or item type
  • Roughly when you're moving
  • Any extras: packing, storage, car shipping

What you get back

  • A starting price for a move like yours
  • The distance, and whether it counts as local or long distance
  • A clear split between the move and optional extras
  • The option to get your exact price from a specialist

Price factors

What affects the cost of your move

Six things decide most of what you'll pay. Knowing them helps you read any quote and spot where you can save.

  • Distance

    Local moves are priced by time, long-distance moves mostly by miles and weight. Crossing state lines also brings federal rules into play.

    Big impact

  • How much you're moving

    More rooms means more weight, a bigger truck and more hours. Clearing out before the move is the easiest way to save.

    Big impact

  • Your moving date

    Summer, weekends and month-ends are busiest. A flexible date can lower the price.

    Medium impact

  • Stairs and access

    Flights of stairs, elevators, long walks from the truck or tight streets all add time.

    Medium impact

  • Heavy or delicate items

    Pianos, pool tables, hot tubs and safes need extra crew, special equipment and care.

    Varies

  • Packing and extras

    Packing, storage and car shipping are optional. Add only what you need.

    Optional

A moving cost calculator turns your ZIP codes, home size, date and extras into a price range in about a minute. For a 1-bedroom home moved 10 road miles, the moving cost calculator shows $380–$960, off peak, with no stairs and no extras. The same home moved 1,000 road miles comes to $1,400–$3,300. It is free, and you see the range without giving an email.

Reading the range a moving cost calculator gives you

Every moving cost calculator result is a range, not a single figure, because two moves of the same size rarely take the same work. The low end fits a light load, easy access at both homes and a crew that keeps moving. The high end fits a fuller home, a long carry to the truck or a slow day. If your rooms are full or your building is awkward, plan on the upper half of the range the moving cost calculator shows.

Behind a local result is crew time: a 1-bedroom home usually needs 2 movers, whose rate together is $100–$150 an hour, truck included. Behind a long-distance result is the size of the shipment and the road miles. Spread over 1,000 miles, the 1-bedroom figure above works out to about $1.45–$3.28 per mile. That is the total divided by the distance, not a rate a moving cost calculator or a mover bills by.

Extras to switch on in the moving cost calculator

The base result covers loading, driving and unloading. Three extras can be added on top, and the moving cost calculator shows the move and the extras apart, so you can see what each one adds.

  • Packing. Having the crew pack adds a charge that grows with the home: $300–$650 for a 1-bedroom home and $800–$1,800 for a 3-bedroom home.
  • Storage. Storage between move-out and move-in is billed on top, and its cost depends on how long your belongings stay and how much space they take.
  • Car shipping. Shipping a car on a long move is priced apart from your household goods and depends mostly on the distance.

Switch each extra on and off in the moving cost calculator to see which ones are worth paying for. Packing is often the largest, and it is also the one you can most easily do yourself over a few evenings.

What sits outside the moving cost calculator result

Some costs of a move are not part of any mover's price, so no moving cost calculator for movers includes them. Budget these on your own:

  • Tips for the crew. Tipping is your choice and paid on the day. The tip calculator below suggests an amount for your crew.
  • Boxes and supplies. If you pack yourself, the boxes, tape and paper are yours to buy. The box estimator below counts them.
  • Parking and building fees. A street permit for the truck, or a fee to reserve a service elevator, depends on your city and your building.
  • Travel and time off. On a long move, fuel, meals and a hotel on the road are yours to pay, along with any unpaid days off work.
  • Deposits and set-up. A security deposit, utility connection fees and cleaning at the old home all land in the same few weeks as the move.

Add these to the moving cost calculator result before you settle on a moving budget, so the figure you plan with is the whole cost of moving and not only the movers' share.

Checking a mover's price against the moving cost calculator

Once written estimates arrive, the moving cost calculator becomes a yardstick. Run it again with the same home size, date and extras each mover priced, then sort the estimates into three groups:

  • Inside the range. The price is in line with what moves like yours cost. Compare what each mover includes before you compare the totals.
  • Well below the range. Ask questions before you book. A price far under the others can be a lowball figure that grows once your goods are on the truck.
  • Well above the range. The estimate may include extras you didn't select, such as packing, stairs or a shuttle truck. Ask for each charge on its own line.

Set the comparison out side by side: the moving cost calculator range in one column and each mover's line items in the next. For an interstate move, FMCSA's Protect Your Move pages list the warning signs to look for in a mover's estimate and explain how to check a mover's registration.

Where a moving cost calculator stops

A moving cost calculator works from home size, not a list of every item, so it can't see a heavy armoire, a garage full of tools or a third-floor walk-up you forgot to mention. Long-distance movers price by weight, and the moving cost calculator uses your home size as a stand-in for it. A common rule of thumb puts a furnished room at around 1,000 pounds, so crowded rooms weigh, and cost, more than the bedroom count suggests.

The moving cost calculator prices moves between US ZIP codes, so a move abroad needs a quote from an international mover. For anything unusual, such as a long storage stay or a building with no truck access, treat the result as a starting point and ask movers to price the details after a survey.

Run the moving cost calculator above again whenever a detail changes: a new date, a different home size or one more extra. It's free and takes about a minute, so you can keep an up-to-date range in hand to judge each quote before you sign.

From estimate to exact price

Five ways to get a quote you can count on

An estimate tells you what to expect. These steps make sure the final bill matches it.

Based on FMCSA moving guidance

  1. List your big items

    Beds, sofas, appliances and anything heavy. They drive weight, crew size and time.

  2. Ask for a survey

    An in-home or video walk-through gives the mover what they need to firm up the price.

  3. Get it in writing

    Know whether your estimate is binding or non-binding before you sign anything.

  4. Check the USDOT number

    For interstate moves, confirm the mover is registered with the FMCSA.

  5. Choose your coverage

    Decide between basic released value and full value protection before moving day.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 8 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • Each result is a range: the low end fits a light load and easy access, the high end a fuller home or a harder day.
  • Sample figures assume 10 or 1,000 road miles, an off-peak date, no stairs and no extras.
  • Tips, supplies, parking permits and travel sit outside the result, so budget them on top.
  • A written estimate far below the range is a reason to ask questions, not a bargain to grab.

Loading and unloading help adds $320–$910, by the calculator's labor-only estimate.

For it

  • Rentals run from 10 ft vans for a studio apartment to 26 ft trucks for larger homes. (HireAHelper)
  • The renter sets the schedule and the pace, and decides whether to bring in help. (HireAHelper)
  • A rental truck can tow a car or extra cargo. (U-Haul)

Against it

  • Rental trucks average only 10 to 12 miles per gallon of unleaded fuel. (moveBuddha)
  • A rental's protection plans cover the truck, not the belongings inside it. (moveBuddha)
  • A rental's per-mile rate can be higher on a Saturday than on a Tuesday. (HireAHelper)

For it

  • The container is delivered to the door, and nothing has to be driven or returned. (HireAHelper)
  • Many container plans come with a month of storage at no extra charge. (HireAHelper)
  • PODS doesn't price by the weight of the belongings. (PODS)

Against it

  • A container needs a driveway, or a city permit to sit on the street. (HireAHelper)
  • PODS doesn't prorate the final month. (HireAHelper)
  • PODS bills each leg separately: delivery, transport to the new city, redelivery and final pickup. (moveBuddha)

For it

  • Experienced crews handle the belongings. (moveBuddha)
  • Full service is the most hands-off way to move: the company packs, loads, drives and unloads. (HireAHelper)
  • Packing supplies are often included. (moveBuddha)

Against it

  • Full service is usually the most expensive way to move. (HireAHelper)
  • Some companies that book moves are brokers, which sell the move on to an actual moving company. (FMCSA)
  • Storage costs extra with full-service movers. (moveBuddha)

The movers' and the hired help's figures are the calculator's estimates for a move off peak; a move from May to September costs more. Crew tips to add to your range

No moving cost calculator for movers counts the tip, since it is your choice and paid on the day. Enter the crew size and how long the job runs to see a fair amount to set aside.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Keeping the final bill close to the estimate

A moving cost calculator assumes the crew can start lifting as soon as it arrives. Tick off these tasks, from booking parking to the final walk-through, so the hours you pay for go on the move itself.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Give every company the same list, so their estimates price the same job.

6 weeks before

  • Moving hours, elevators, loading docks and gates. If one wants the company's certificate of insurance, ask the company to send it ahead.

4 weeks before

  • Whether it takes a deposit, when the rest is due, and which payment methods it accepts.

2 weeks before

  • Get a name and a direct number, not only the main office line.

1 week before

  • Ask for a phone number that will be answered on moving day.

  • Ask the building or the city whether you need a permit or cones.

The day before

  • Eat down the frozen food in the weeks before, so little is left to throw away.

  • Have the estimate and the company's number where you can reach them.

Moving day

  • Note any damage on the paperwork before you sign for delivery.

  • Look high and low: top shelves, under sinks, the attic and the garage.

  • Point out anything fragile, very heavy or going to a particular room.

  • FMCSA's advice: if you can't be there, ask someone you know to act for you.

    Source: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration

After the move

  • Then the kitchen basics; the rest can wait a day.

  • Send photos and a list of what's damaged or missing as soon as you find it.

Questions

Moving cost calculator FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How do you estimate the cost of a move?

Start with a moving cost calculator: enter both ZIP codes, your home size, the date and any extras to get a range. A studio apartment moved 10 road miles, off peak with no stairs or extras, comes to $280–$740. Then add the costs movers don't charge for, such as tips, supplies and travel, and ask movers for written estimates to firm it up.

Is the moving cost calculator free, and does it need an email?

It's free, and the range appears on the page without an email or a sign-up. The moving cost calculator takes about a minute: you enter ZIP codes, home size, date and extras, and the price range shows straight away. Asking to be put in touch with a mover afterwards is up to you.

How much should I expect to pay to move?

With movers, a 3-bedroom home moved 10 road miles costs $1,150–$2,850, and moved 1,000 road miles it costs $4,000–$8,550, both off peak with no stairs or extras. Smaller homes cost less and bigger ones more. Run the moving cost calculator with your own ZIP codes and date for a range that fits your move.

How is an average moving cost calculated?

For a local move, multiply the crew size by the hourly rate and the hours: one mover typically costs $50–$75 an hour, truck included, so a 3-mover crew costs three times that. For a long move, the sum uses the weight of the shipment and the miles instead. A moving cost calculator does both sums from your inputs, and gives a range rather than one average figure.

Can a moving cost calculator price a move by weight?

Not directly. The moving cost calculator asks for your home size and uses that as a stand-in for weight. Movers weigh a long-distance shipment, or estimate it after a survey, so their figure can differ if your rooms are fuller or emptier than most. Tell each mover about heavy pieces, such as a gun safe or a piano, at the survey.
